intro.headline: Help shape the new website
intro.body: We are rebuilding the website, and the people who work here every day should shape it. This takes about 10 minutes. There are no wrong answers. Say what you actually think.
intro.privacyNote: Your name and email are collected so we can follow up on great ideas and make sure we hear from every area. Your answers will be shared with the project team.

confirmation.headline: Thank you.
confirmation.body: Your input is in. We're reading every response, and what you shared will shape the website directions we bring back.

sections.title: First, who are you?
sections.blurb: So we can make sure every part of the company is represented.

questions.label: Your name
Your email
Your area
How long have you been here?

sections.title: The site today
sections.blurb: Think about the website as it is right now. Be honest. This part is the most useful thing you can give us.

questions.label: What works on the current website?
questions.placeholder: Pages you use, things people find easily, anything that feels right...

questions.label: What frustrates you about it, or what do you hear people complain about?
questions.placeholder: Hard to find, out of date, confusing, slow, not us...

questions.label: How well does the site serve someone who has never heard of us?
What must NOT change?
questions.placeholder: Anything on the current site you would fight to keep.

sections.title: What the site is for
sections.blurb: A website can't do everything well. Help us decide what matters most.

questions.label: If the website only did three things really well, what should they be?

options.label: Explain what we do in a few seconds
Make it easy to call, book or ask for a quote
Prove we're good at it (reviews, results, past work)
Help people find the right service or product
Attract good people to work here

questions.label: Who does the website most need to serve?

options.label: People who have never heard of us
People comparing us with a competitor
People a customer sent our way

sections.title: Getting in touch
sections.blurb: The website should move someone from curious to talking with us, then make the next step obvious.

questions.label: How clearly does the website show someone what to do next?
When someone is ready to talk, how easy is it to reach the right person?
Where do people get stuck between finding us and becoming a customer?
questions.placeholder: What you see in your role, what customers tell you...

questions.label: What's one thing the website could do to make your job easier?

sections.title: Pages your team updates
sections.blurb: A site only stays good if it's easy to keep current. Tell us what your team needs to change and how often.

questions.label: What does your team need to post or update on the website, and how often?
questions.placeholder: Hours, prices, staff, events, job openings, news...

questions.label: What's hardest about getting something updated on the site today?

sections.title: Homepage concept
sections.blurb: We've built a first draft of the new homepage. Open it, scroll through, then come back and tell us what you think. It's a starting point, not a final design.

questions.label: How well does this direction fit us?
What works?
What's missing or feels off?

sections.title: How it should feel
sections.blurb: For each pair, set two markers: where the website is today, and where it should be. It's fine if they're in the same place.

questions.label: Pick exactly 5 words the website should feel like
Now pick exactly 3 words it should never feel like

sections.title: Sites you admire
sections.blurb: Examples beat adjectives. In our industry or not, any website that does something well counts.

questions.label: Websites that point the right direction

fields.label: What do you like about it?

sections.title: A year out
sections.blurb: Last one. This is the answer we'll read out loud.

questions.label: Finish this sentence
questions.prefix: A year after the new website launches, I hope people say it
